record.paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
record.original_question: Are Dirac’s Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity, formulated using the original metric variables, and the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, which reparametrizes gravitational variables using lapse and shift functions together with the spatial three-metric, equivalent Hamiltonian descriptions of the same theory despite the claim that the transformation from the four-metric variables to ADM variables is not canonical in the usual phase space?

evidence.quote: In spite of decades passed from the famous papers by Dirac and ADM, there are unsolved problems. Namely, are the Dirac and ADM formulations equivalent to each other?

the authors claim that the formulation by Dirac and that by ADM are not equivalent since these two formulations are related by a non-canonical transformation of phase space variables from the 4-metrics g_{μν} to the lapse and shift functions N, N_i and the 3-metrics γ_{ij}.
It returns us to the questions: Are the Dirac and ADM formulations really non-equivalent to each other?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity on a globally hyperbolic spacetime, given by the Einstein–Hilbert action

S = (1/16πG) ∫ R √(−g) d⁴x,

with dynamical field the Lorentzian four-metric g_{μν}.

Two standard Hamiltonian formulations of this theory are:

(A) Dirac's formulation. Carry out the Legendre transform directly in the variables g_{μν}, treating the ten components of the four-metric as configuration variables, introducing momenta π^{μν} conjugate to g_{μν}, and applying Dirac's algorithm for constrained Hamiltonian systems to obtain primary and secondary constraints together with a total Hamiltonian.

(B) ADM formulation. Perform a 3+1 decomposition of g_{μν} into the lapse N, the shift vector N^i, and the spatial three-metric γ_{ij} via
  g_{00} = −N² + γ_{ij} N^i N^j,  g_{0i} = γ_{ij} N^j,  g_{ij} = γ_{ij},
take (N, N^i, γ_{ij}) as configuration variables, and carry out the Dirac–Bergmann constrained-Hamiltonian analysis, yielding the familiar Hamiltonian and momentum (diffeomorphism) constraints.

A change of variables (g_{μν}) ↦ (N, N^i, γ_{ij}) is well-defined and invertible at the Lagrangian level, but extending it to a transformation of the phase-space variables (g_{μν}, π^{μν}) ↦ (N, N^i, γ_{ij}, π_N, π_{N^i}, π^{ij}_γ) is, in the standard phase space, not a canonical transformation: the induced map does not preserve the symplectic structure (Poisson brackets), and the gauge symmetries generated by the constraints in the two formulations differ.

Question. Are the Dirac formulation (A) and the ADM formulation (B) nevertheless equivalent Hamiltonian descriptions of General Relativity, in the sense of describing the same physical theory with the same gauge structure and the same reduced phase space? In particular, is the apparent non-canonicity of the change of variables relating them an artifact that can be removed by a suitable extension or modification of the phase space, or does it reflect a genuine inequivalence of the two Hamiltonian formulations?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been actively debated. One line of work (Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin and collaborators) argues that the Dirac and ADM Hamiltonian formulations are genuinely inequivalent because the change of variables to lapse/shift/three-metric is non-canonical and changes the gauge symmetry from full four-diffeomorphisms to a different (field-dependent) symmetry. A counter-line (e.g. Frolov–Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin, Shestakova) proposes that the non-canonicity disappears in an extended phase space where gauge degrees of freedom are treated on equal footing, recovering canonical equivalence. There is no universally accepted resolution, so the problem is best characterized as partially solved / actively discussed rather than definitively closed.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian symmetries of the ADM action. Do we need a solution to the 'non-canonicity puzzle'?
status_evidence.snippet: The two symmetries are distinct, and correspondingly the Hamiltonians are not equivalent and the field variables are not related by a canonical transformation.
status_evidence.claim: Argues Dirac and ADM Hamiltonian formulations are not equivalent and not related by a canonical transformation.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian formulation for the theory of gravity and canonical transformations in extended phase space
status_evidence.snippet: The ADM-like transformation is shown to be canonical in an extended phase space where gauge degrees of freedom are introduced on equal footing.
status_evidence.claim: Proposes resolution via extended phase space, restoring canonical equivalence.

status_evidence.title: The Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity: myths and reality
status_evidence.snippet: Detailed analysis claiming that Dirac's and ADM's Hamiltonian formulations are inequivalent, with different gauge symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: Claims genuine inequivalence between Dirac's and ADM's Hamiltonian formulations of GR.
